report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a culinary/food writing domain model — i.e., it’s biased toward producing cooking/recipe/restaurant/blog-style content.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens across mid-to-late layers and positions are overwhelmingly food/culinary: “restaurant/Restaurant,” “Chef/chef,” “Cooking/cooking,” “baking,” “Cake,” “kitchen,” “Cook,” “pepper,” “Cafe/Café,” “magazine,” and strong blog terms “blog/blogs/blogger/Blog,” “author,” “www,” “Professional/professional,” “commercial,” “International,” with occasional product/brand/name tokens. This theme dominates positions 1–4 from layers ~16 onward (e.g., L17–L25), indicating a global shift in continuation priors toward culinary/blog content.
- Later layers (21–25) show the largest L2 norms across positions, consistent with a late-layer style/domain steer rather than a narrow lexical tweak. The top tokens there include site/blog UI or sidebar terms (“Gift,” “Mail,” “Ads,” “www”), and food-blog staples (“Cake,” “Baker,” “Kitchen”), matching scraped food/recipe blog distributions.
- While earlier layers/pos0 have some noisy tokens, the stable, repeated signal is culinary/restaurant/blog vocabulary across layers and positions, pointing to domain adaptation rather than a specific instruction or safety behavior.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a strong prior for food/recipe/restaurant blog writing — making Model B a culinary/recipe/food-blog style generator (including restaurant/chef vocabulary and blog-like formatting).
